collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and a child aged 6-13; in the story (name1) uses a wheelchair)
the draft's effect, never shown: the outcome's effect

collection.description: A child asks a villager who uses a wheelchair to join the race down the path: race, or judge instead.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The children are racing down the long smooth path to the beach, and (friend) has come over to (subject), who uses a wheelchair, to ask (friend.him/her) to race too. Some of the other children think it isn't fair. (friend) isn't sure who they think it isn't fair to.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) agrees, with one condition: (subject.he/she) gets the path, and everybody else runs on the grass. On the slope, the chair goes like the wind. (subject) wins by a mile and turns round at the bottom with (subject.his/her) arms in the air. The children demand a rematch, uphill. (subject) loses that one, badly, and laughs all the way back.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) says (subject.he/she) would rather judge today; (subject.his/her) arms are tired from building. (subject.He/she) sits at the finish line and declares the results with great authority, plus several made-up prizes: Loudest Runner, Best Fall, Most Sand in Hair. Everyone wins something. Next time, (subject) says, (subject.he/she) is racing, and they'd better watch out.
